title: Newmark Facilitates $215.8 Million in Refinancing for Waypoint Residential Multifamily Portfolio in Florida
summary: Newmark announces the Company has arranged $215.8 million in bridge refinancing for Waypoint Residential’s five-property, 1,274-unit multifamily portfolio…
body_markdown:
**September 2, 2026 9:00 AM**
Newmark announces the Company has arranged $215.8 million in bridge refinancing for Waypoint Residential’s five-property, 1,274-unit multifamily portfolio spanning key markets throughout Florida.


Newmark Vice Chairman[Matthew Williams](https://www.nmrk.com/people/matthew-williams) and Vice President[Rob Wright](https://www.nmrk.com/people/rob-wright) secured the construction takeout bridge financing through Benefit Street Partners, with support from Managing Directors[James Maynard](https://www.nmrk.com/people/james-maynard) and[Kyle Schlitt](https://www.nmrk.com/people/kyle-schlitt) .


“The size and complexity of this portfolio required a coordinated financing strategy across five distinct Florida markets, each with its own lease-up and stabilization dynamics,” said Williams. “Our extensive lender outreach generated significant interest from a broad range of capital providers and provided Waypoint with multiple financing alternatives. The resulting bridge structure gives the ownership additional runway to optimize the portfolio while maintaining flexibility around its longer-term capital strategy.”


The portfolio comprises five newly constructed, luxury garden-style multifamily communities in Vero Beach, Port St. Lucie, Palm Bay, Davenport and Gainesville. Three properties are located along Florida’s Treasure Coast and Space Coast and were completed in 2024, benefiting from continued population and employment growth, a moderating new supply pipeline and proximity to major healthcare, aerospace, advanced manufacturing and logistics employers.


The remaining two properties include The Bradley at Lake Wilson in Davenport, which benefits from access to Orlando’s employment centers, tourism corridor and major transportation infrastructure, and The Marlow Gainesville, located near the University of Florida and UF Health, two of the area’s largest economic drivers.


According to[Newmark Research](https://www.nmrk.com/insights/market-report/1q26-u-s-multifamily-capital-markets-conditions-trends) , U.S. multifamily fundamentals continued to strengthen in 1Q26, with absorption reaching 93,277 units, approximately 40% above the long-term average. At the same time, new supply continued to moderate, with 75,205 units delivered during the quarter, 53.1% below the 3Q24 peak, while annual inventory growth slowed to a 10-quarter low.
